findings.issue: The new stale-write guard skips the post-render DOM write on every BOUND date field whenever the keystroke changed Value, because Blazor's own diff has already written the formatted text into the element before OnAfterRenderAsync runs: el.value is then the formatted string ('12/50/9') while `expected` is the pre-format raw text ('125/09'), so they can never match and the write — including the caret restore — is dropped. Reproduced live over CDP on the running host (/gallery, whose date field is `@bind-Value="_dateValue"`, Gallery.razor:35), with setInputValue instrumented: typing 1,2,0,9 then setting the caret to index 2 and typing '5' logs {"before":"12/50/9","value":"12/50/9","caret":4,"expected":"125/09","skipped":true} and the caret ends at 7 (end of field). With the guard bypassed at runtime in the same page and the identical keystrokes, the caret ends at 4. This regresses the accepted mid-string caret fix that the previous review verified live ('caret stays beside the inserted digit — finding 3 works in the real host') for ALL mid-string editing (insertion and deletion) of a bound date field, in exchange for closing a race the same review described as unreachable by a human. bUnit cannot catch it because its JSInterop mock never executes app.js.
findings.fix: Compare against both texts the element may legitimately hold: in wakeelUi.setInputValue change the early return to `if (expected !== undefined && expected !== null && el.value !== expected && el.value !== value) { return; }`. When Blazor already wrote the formatted value the write proceeds and is a no-op on the value but still fixes the caret; when a newer keystroke has moved the element on, el.value matches neither and the stale write is still skipped. Keep the existing clamp and the fourth WInput argument unchanged. Re-verify live over CDP on /gallery: 1,2,0,9 then caret to index 2 then '5' must give value '12/50/9' with selectionStart 4, and re-run verify3's zero-delay scripted burst (1,2,0,9,2,0,2,6) to confirm no digits are dropped.

findings.issue: The rollback sweep cannot remove the residue of the write that actually failed: ActivationService adds a hash to `writtenVaultHashes` only after VaultStore.Write returns, and Write creates `<vaultfile>.tmp`, writes and flushes it, then File.Move's it into place. If the move or the write throws — a full disk, the exact failure ActivationService special-cases, or the blocked path the new walkthrough test creates — the flushed, encrypted temporary file stays in the vault folder and is in no list, so RollBack never touches it. Those bytes are sealed with the vault key that was wiped with the abandoned key file: the same dead, unaccountable bytes the finding set out to eliminate.
findings.fix: In VaultStore.Write wrap the stream write and the File.Move in try/catch, and on failure `File.Delete(temporary)` (swallowing IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException exactly as VaultStore.Delete does) before rethrowing; additionally, in ActivationService.RollBack delete `_paths.VaultFilePath(hash) + ".tmp"` alongside each collected hash. Extend the new walkthrough test with `Assert.False(File.Exists(world.Paths.VaultFilePath(guideHash) + ".tmp"))` after the rollback.

findings.issue: Only the mandatory half of the finding is closed. The fix text also asks for the memory to be dropped 'when LoginService.OpenSessionAsync resets the profile counters'; the builder reported no clean seam exists, but LoginService.Profile() is public and SignInProfile.FailedAttempts (SignInProfile.cs:47) is exactly the reset counter. As it stands, a successful password sign-in zeroes the counters while RecoveryService keeps remembering the last wrong code, so that one code text can still be retried for free afterwards.
findings.fix: At the top of CountWrongCode, before the dedup comparison: `if (_login.Profile().FailedAttempts == 0) { _lastCountedCode = null; }`. Cover it in FirstRunWalkthroughTests: count one wrong code, sign in successfully with the password, then re-submit the same wrong code and assert FailedAttempts rose to 1.

findings.issue: The new W05 idle lock-out timer has no test at all. FixedTime (line 144) overrides only GetUtcNow, so W05Login's `Time.CreateTimer` falls through to the base TimeProvider and creates a real 15-second system timer that no test ever fires; the only lock-out test, The_sign_in_button_comes_back_by_itself_once_the_wait_is_over, still drives the typing path (it calls password.ValueChanged). StartLockTimer, CheckLockTimer and Dispose are therefore unexercised — if the timer were never started, or the callback threw, the suite would stay green.
findings.fix: Give FixedTime a controllable CreateTimer (return a small internal ITimer that records the callback and exposes a Fire() method, no new NuGet package needed), then add a test: render W05Login with LockedUntil set, assert «دخول» disabled, clear LockedUntil in the profile, fire the timer, and assert the danger card is gone and the button is enabled without any keystroke — plus that the timer is disposed when the component is.

missing_spec_items: verify2-firstrun.json finding 4 (RecoveryService): the second clause of the prescribed fix — 'and ideally also when LoginService.OpenSessionAsync resets the profile counters' — is not implemented. The builder disclosed it in open_issues; a clean seam does exist (see the low finding).

LIVE REPRODUCTION OF THE MEDIUM FINDING. On the same host I navigated to /gallery, wrapped wakeelUi.setInputValue with a logger (page-only, no file changed) and drove real Input.dispatchKeyEvent keystrokes. Mid-string insertion with the guard: value '12/50/9', caret 7, log entry skipped:true (expected '125/09' vs a DOM already holding '12/50/9' from Blazor's diff). Same keystrokes with the guard bypassed at runtime: value '12/50/9', caret 4 — i.e. the guard, not anything else, is what moved the caret to the end. Verified the field is bound (Gallery.razor:35 @bind-Value), which is why Blazor rewrites the DOM before OnAfterRenderAsync. The rejected-character path is unaffected (Value does not change there, so el.value still equals the raw text and the write proceeds).

WHAT IS CORRECTLY CLOSED. (1) W07 renders the RecoveredNotSignedIn sentence in the new-sheet branch as a Warning WCard, and in that branch _error can only ever be that sentence (SubmitAsync nulls _error first, and every failure path returns before _newSheet is set). (2) ConfirmLabel/ConfirmIcon/ConfirmAsync are all gated on `_newSheet is null && !_recoveredWithoutSession`, and CloseAsync's `recovered` flag stays correct. (3) ActivationService threads writtenVaultHashes through StoreAttachmentsAsync/StoreAsync and RollBack sweeps them via the new VaultStore.Delete; the walkthrough test blocks the guide's vault slot, asserts the logo blob is gone and that a clean retry works — it fails without the sweep, so it is real behaviour, not a tautology (only the `.tmp` residue of the failing write is missed — low finding 2). (4) RecoveryService clears _lastCountedCode on the Success path only (the RecoveredNotSignedIn return does not clear it; defensible, since the finding named the Success result). (5) W05Login starts a LockService.TickInterval timer on both entries into the locked state, stops it on every exit and in Dispose, and CheckLockTimer runs through InvokeAsync so touching state is safe — but it is untested (low finding 4). (6) E2E: the self-referential assertion is replaced by a documented tolerance plus a TryParse on the artefact, the CDP session is detached in the same finally, and WaitForPageAsync now throws a plain InvalidOperationException — I checked InitializeAsync's catch is a catch-all, so DisposeAsync still kills the process and nothing leaks; AppLaunchTimeoutTests (a different throw site) still passes. (7) App.xaml.cs got only the documentation comment; the unconditional clear is unchanged.

SCOPE AND STYLE. The diff touches only the twelve files the package claims; nothing else in them changed (I read every hunk). No new NuGet package, no edit to Directory.*.props, the solution or docs beyond the progress file. No new user-facing string was introduced — the warning card reuses Ar.FirstRun.Recovery.SucceededNotSignedIn — so Arabic-only text, no technical terms or error codes, and the sheet-action buttons keep their Tooltip attributes. Identifiers, comments and XML docs are English (product name الوكيل and quoted UI strings aside, matching the existing house style). I compared the implemented W05 and W07 against design/exports/preview/light/W/W05 and preview/dark/W/W07: structure, step indicator, field order and RTL all match; the new warning card is a failure state the design does not draw and reuses the existing WCard variant.

ON THE E2E BASELINE (not a finding — the spec asked for exactly this): Assert.InRange(33.30 +/- 0.5) turns a deliberately threshold-free harness into one that will fail on a machine whose sub-pixel rendering differs by more than 0.5 pp, or after any legitimate W08 export refresh. Whoever changes W08 or its export must update BaselineDiffPercentage in the same commit; the comment in the test says so for later B1-B8 packages.
